steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: RAW files contain far more data than JPEGs — they allow greater adjustment in post-processing without quality loss.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Levels and curves control tonal range and contrast; colour balance adjusts warmth/coolness across the image.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dodging (lightening) and burning (darkening) specific areas directs the viewer's attention — used by photographers since the darkroom era.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethical considerations: photojournalism requires minimal manipulation; fine art photography allows creative transformation — know the boundaries of your genre.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring digital editing and manipulation. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with digital editing and manipulation. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with digital editing and manipulation. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to digital editing and manipulation, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
